title.en: CBD Architecture, Protocols and Benefit Sharing
title.te: CBD నిర్మాణం, Protocols మరియు Benefit Sharing

paragraphs.en: A convention is a principal international treaty negotiated by countries. Its legal obligations apply to a country after it becomes a Party through ratification, accession or another accepted procedure. A protocol is a separate legal instrument made under a convention to provide more detailed rules for a particular subject. Joining the parent convention does not automatically make a country Party to every protocol under it.
paragraphs.te: Countries కలిసి negotiate చేసే ప్రధాన international treatyని Convention అంటారు. ఒక country ratification లేదా accession ద్వారా Party అయిన తర్వాతే ఆ treatyలోని legal obligations దానికి వర్తిస్తాయి. Conventionలోని ఒక specific subjectకు మరింత detailed rules ఇచ్చే separate legal instrumentను Protocol అంటారు. Parent Conventionలో Party అయినంత మాత్రాన, దాని కింద ఉన్న ప్రతి Protocolలోనూ automaticగా Party అయినట్లు కాదు.

paragraphs.en: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was adopted and opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit on 5 June 1992. It entered into force on 29 December 1993. Its three objectives are the conservation of biological diversity, the sustainable use of its components, and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources. The third objective is commonly called access and benefit-sharing (ABS).
paragraphs.te: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)ను 5 June 1992న Rio Earth Summitలో adopt చేసి, signature కోసం open చేశారు. ఇది 29 December 1993న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. CBDకి మూడు objectives ఉన్నాయి: biodiversity conservation; biodiversity componentsను sustainableగా use చేయడం; genetic resourcesను ఉపయోగించడం వల్ల వచ్చే benefitsను fair and equitableగా share చేయడం. మూడవ objectiveను సాధారణంగా Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) అంటారు.

paragraphs.en: CBD Article 6 requires each Party, according to its conditions and capabilities, to develop national strategies, plans or programmes for conservation and sustainable use, or adapt existing ones for that purpose. These are commonly presented as a National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP). Aichi Target 17 later asked Parties to prepare, adopt and begin implementing updated NBSAPs by 2015; it did not create the original planning obligation.
paragraphs.te: CBD Article 6 ప్రకారం, ప్రతి Party తన పరిస్థితులు మరియు సామర్థ్యానికి అనుగుణంగా biodiversity conservation, sustainable use కోసం national strategies, plans లేదా programmes రూపొందించాలి; లేదా ఇప్పటికే ఉన్న వాటిని ఈ purposeకు adapt చేయాలి. వీటిని సాధారణంగా National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP)గా రూపొందిస్తారు. తరువాత వచ్చిన Aichi Target 17, 2015 నాటికి updated NBSAPను prepare చేసి, adopt చేసి, implementation ప్రారంభించాలని చెప్పింది. కానీ national biodiversity planning obligationను మొదట సృష్టించింది Article 6నే.

paragraphs.en: The Rio process produced different instruments for different environmental problems. The CBD addresses biodiversity and the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) addresses climate change; both were opened for signature at Rio in 1992. Agenda 21 also called for negotiations on desertification. That process produced the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), which was adopted in 1994 and is legally binding. CBD, UNFCCC and UNCCD are therefore known together as the three Rio Conventions, although UNCCD was adopted after the Summit.
paragraphs.te: Rio process అన్ని environmental problemsకు ఒకే treatyని ఇవ్వలేదు. Biodiversity కోసం CBD, climate change కోసం UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) ఏర్పడ్డాయి; ఇవి రెండూ 1992 Rio Summitలో signature కోసం open అయ్యాయి. Desertificationపై treaty negotiations జరగాలని Agenda 21 సూచించింది. ఆ process ద్వారా legally binding UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) 1994లో adopt అయింది. అందుకే CBD, UNFCCC, UNCCDలను కలిపి three Rio Conventions అంటారు; అయితే UNCCD Summit తరువాత adopt అయిందని గుర్తుంచుకోవాలి.

paragraphs.en: Ramsar, CITES and CMS are not protocols under the CBD. Each is an independent convention with its own treaty text, Parties and governing body. The Like-Minded Megadiverse Countries (LMMC), formed in 2002, is different again: it is a negotiating coalition of biodiversity-rich countries. India was among its founding members. The group coordinates positions in biodiversity negotiations, especially on ABS and traditional knowledge. Membership of LMMC is a diplomatic arrangement; the scientific description of a country as megadiverse is a separate idea.
paragraphs.te: Ramsar, CITES, CMS అనేవి CBD కింద Protocols కావు. ప్రతి ఒక్కటి own treaty text, Parties, governing body ఉన్న independent Convention. Like-Minded Megadiverse Countries (LMMC) దీనికంటే వేరు. 2002లో ఏర్పడిన ఈ group, biodiversity-rich countries కలిసి negotiationsలో common position తీసుకోవడానికి ఉపయోగించే coalition. India దీని founding membersలో ఒకటి. ముఖ్యంగా ABS, traditional knowledge వంటి issuesపై ఈ group coordination చేస్తుంది. LMMC membership ఒక diplomatic arrangement; ఒక countryని scientificగా megadiverse country అనడం వేరే concept.

paragraphs.en: The CBD has two protocols: the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing. It also has the Nagoya–Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol under Cartagena; this should not be counted as a third stand-alone CBD protocol. Cartagena was adopted on 29 January 2000 and entered into force on 11 September 2003. It deals mainly with the safe transfer, handling and use of living modified organisms (LMOs) resulting from modern biotechnology, especially where transboundary movement may affect biodiversity and human health.
paragraphs.te: CBD కింద రెండు Protocols ఉన్నాయి: Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety మరియు Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing. Cartagena కింద Nagoya–Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol కూడా ఉంది; దాన్ని third stand-alone CBD Protocolగా count చేయకూడదు. Cartagena Protocolను 29 January 2000న adopt చేశారు; 11 September 2003న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. Modern biotechnology ద్వారా ఏర్పడిన living modified organisms (LMOs) transfer, handling, use సురక్షితంగా ఉండేలా ఇది rules ఇస్తుంది. ముఖ్యంగా transboundary movement వల్ల biodiversityకు, human healthకు కలిగే risksపై ఇది దృష్టి పెడుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: Cartagena follows a precautionary approach. When relevant scientific information is insufficient, an importing Party may still take a protective decision about an LMO. This does not mean that the Protocol creates one universal rule placing the burden of proof on the same side in every case. Its Advance Informed Agreement procedure applies to specified LMOs intended for intentional introduction into the environment; it does not apply identically to every movement or use of an LMO.
paragraphs.te: Cartagena Protocol precautionary approachను అనుసరిస్తుంది. Relevant scientific information సరిపోకపోయినా, importing Party ఒక LMOపై protective decision తీసుకోవచ్చు. కానీ ప్రతి caseలో burden of proof ఎప్పుడూ ఒకే sideపై ఉంటుందని Protocol చెప్పదు. దీని Advance Informed Agreement procedure, environmentలో intentionally release చేయబోయే specified LMOsకు వర్తిస్తుంది. ప్రతి LMO movement లేదా useకు ఇదే procedure ఒకే విధంగా వర్తించదు.

paragraphs.en: The Nagoya Protocol was adopted at CBD COP10 on 29 October 2010 and entered into force on 12 October 2014. It implements ABS by providing rules for access, benefit-sharing and compliance. Where the provider country's domestic ABS law requires it, access to genetic resources is based on Prior Informed Consent (PIC), and benefit-sharing is arranged through Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT). The Protocol also addresses traditional knowledge associated with genetic resources and the rights of Indigenous peoples and local communities under applicable domestic law.
paragraphs.te: Nagoya Protocolను CBD COP10లో 29 October 2010న adopt చేశారు; ఇది 12 October 2014న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. Access, benefit-sharing, complianceకు rules ఇవ్వడం ద్వారా ABSను అమలు చేస్తుంది. Provider country domestic ABS law కోరినప్పుడు, genetic resourcesకు access పొందడానికి Prior Informed Consent (PIC) అవసరం. Benefits ఎలా share చేయాలో Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT)లో నిర్ణయిస్తారు. Genetic resourcesతో associated traditional knowledge, Indigenous peoples మరియు local communities rightsను కూడా applicable domestic law ప్రకారం Protocol address చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: The Nagoya–Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol was adopted on 15 October 2010 and entered into force on 5 March 2018. It provides international rules and procedures on liability and redress when damage to biodiversity results from LMOs whose origin is a transboundary movement. Its focus is response measures for damage; it is not the general ABS instrument.
paragraphs.te: Nagoya–Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocolను 15 October 2010న adopt చేశారు; ఇది 5 March 2018న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. Transboundary movement నుంచి వచ్చిన LMOs వల్ల biodiversityకు damage జరిగితే liability, redress మరియు response measures ఎలా ఉండాలో ఇది rules ఇస్తుంది. ఇది general ABS instrument కాదు; LMO damageకు response దీని main focus.

paragraphs.en: CBD COP15 adopted the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) in Montreal in December 2022. It is a framework adopted through a CBD COP decision, not a separate treaty. It contains four long-term goals for 2050 and 23 action-oriented targets for 2030. Countries implement it through national targets, policies and updated NBSAPs.
paragraphs.te: CBD COP15, December 2022లో Montrealలో Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF)ను adopt చేసింది. ఇది CBD COP decision ద్వారా adopt చేసిన framework; separate treaty కాదు. ఇందులో 2050 కోసం four long-term goals, 2030 కోసం 23 action-oriented targets ఉన్నాయి. Countries తమ national targets, policies, updated NBSAPs ద్వారా దీన్ని implement చేస్తాయి.

paragraphs.en: Before the KMGBF, the Strategic Plan for Biodiversity 2011–2020 contained 20 Aichi Biodiversity Targets. They were adopted at COP10 in Nagoya in 2010, at the same meeting that adopted the Nagoya Protocol. The fifth Global Biodiversity Outlook concluded that none of the 20 targets had been fully achieved at the global level by 2020, although six were partially achieved. This means the world made some progress, but not enough to meet any target completely.
paragraphs.te: KMGBFకు ముందు Strategic Plan for Biodiversity 2011–2020లో 20 Aichi Biodiversity Targets ఉండేవి. 2010లో Nagoyaలో జరిగిన COP10లో వీటిని adopt చేశారు; అదే meetingలో Nagoya Protocol కూడా adopt అయింది. Fifth Global Biodiversity Outlook ప్రకారం, 2020 నాటికి 20 targetsలో ఒక్కటీ global levelలో fully achieve కాలేదు; six targets partially achieve అయ్యాయి. అంటే progress అసలు జరగలేదని కాదు; ఏ targetను పూర్తిగా చేరుకునేంత progress జరగలేదని అర్థం.

paragraphs.en: KMGBF Target 3 is known as the 30×30 target. By 2030, at least 30 per cent of terrestrial and inland-water areas, and at least 30 per cent of coastal and marine areas, should be effectively conserved and managed. Priority includes areas important for biodiversity and ecosystem functions and services. The conservation network should be ecologically representative, well connected and equitably governed, and integrated into wider landscapes and seascapes.
paragraphs.te: KMGBF Target 3ను 30×30 target అంటారు. 2030 నాటికి terrestrial and inland-water areasలో కనీసం 30%, coastal and marine areasలో కనీసం 30%ను effectively conserve చేసి manage చేయాలి. Biodiversity, ecosystem functions మరియు servicesకు ముఖ్యమైన areasకు priority ఇవ్వాలి. ఈ conservation network ecological regionsకు representation ఇవ్వాలి, well connectedగా ఉండాలి, equitable governance కలిగి ఉండాలి, wider landscapes మరియు seascapesతో కలిసిపని చేయాలి.

paragraphs.en: Target 3 can be implemented through protected areas and other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs), while recognizing relevant Indigenous and traditional territories where applicable. An OECM is a geographically defined area outside a formally designated protected area. Its governance and management must nevertheless produce sustained, long-term in-situ conservation of biodiversity. Conservation may be its primary aim, a secondary aim, or an additional result of management, but the biodiversity outcome must be real and lasting.
paragraphs.te: Target 3ను protected areasతో పాటు Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs) ద్వారా కూడా implement చేయవచ్చు. Applicable సందర్భాల్లో relevant Indigenous and traditional territoriesను కూడా recognize చేయవచ్చు. OECM అనేది formally designated protected areaకు బయట ఉన్న geographically defined area. అయినా అక్కడి governance, management వల్ల biodiversityకు sustained, long-term in-situ conservation outcome రావాలి. Conservation అక్కడ primary aim కావచ్చు, secondary aim కావచ్చు, లేదా management వల్ల వచ్చే additional result కావచ్చు; కానీ biodiversity benefit నిజంగా, దీర్ఘకాలంగా ఉండాలి.

paragraphs.en: KMGBF Target 18 concerns incentives, including subsidies, that harm biodiversity. It called for their identification by 2025 and for them to be eliminated, phased out or reformed in a fair and effective manner. By 2030, harmful incentives should be reduced by at least US$500 billion per year, beginning with the most harmful, while positive incentives for biodiversity are increased.
paragraphs.te: KMGBF Target 18, biodiversityకు harm చేసే incentives మరియు subsidiesపై దృష్టి పెడుతుంది. వాటిని 2025 నాటికి identify చేసి, fair and effectiveగా eliminate, phase out లేదా reform చేయాలని చెబుతుంది. Most harmful incentivesతో ప్రారంభించి, 2030 నాటికి వాటిని సంవత్సరానికి కనీసం US$500 billion మేర reduce చేయాలి. అదే సమయంలో biodiversityకు positive incentivesను scale up చేయాలి.

paragraphs.en: KMGBF Target 19 calls for at least US$200 billion per year to be mobilized for biodiversity from all sources by 2030. Within this total effort, biodiversity-related international finance from developed countries and other countries voluntarily assuming similar obligations to developing countries should reach at least US$20 billion per year by 2025 and US$30 billion per year by 2030. The target includes domestic, international, public, private and innovative sources of finance.
paragraphs.te: KMGBF Target 19 ప్రకారం, 2030 నాటికి biodiversity కోసం all sources నుంచి సంవత్సరానికి కనీసం US$200 billion mobilize చేయాలి. ఇందులో developed countries మరియు similar obligationsను voluntarily తీసుకునే countries నుంచి developing countriesకు వచ్చే biodiversity-related international finance, 2025 నాటికి సంవత్సరానికి కనీసం US$20 billion, 2030 నాటికి US$30 billion చేరాలి. Domestic, international, public, private మరియు innovative finance sources అన్నీ ఈ targetలో భాగం.

paragraphs.en: Digital sequence information (DSI) is genetic sequence information that can be stored, shared and used digitally without transferring the physical biological material each time. Because this use does not always involve a new physical-access transaction with a provider country, applying a purely bilateral ABS model can be difficult. The CBD therefore created a multilateral mechanism for sharing benefits from the use of DSI on genetic resources.
paragraphs.te: Digital Sequence Information (DSI) అంటే genetic sequenceకు సంబంధించిన informationను digital formలో store, share, use చేయడం. ప్రతి use సమయంలో physical biological materialను provider country నుంచి మళ్లీ తీసుకోవాల్సిన అవసరం ఉండదు. అందువల్ల purely bilateral ABS modelను digital useకు apply చేయడం కష్టమవుతుంది. ఈ gapను address చేయడానికి, genetic resourcesపై DSI use నుంచి వచ్చే benefitsను share చేసే multilateral mechanismను CBD ఏర్పాటు చేసింది.

paragraphs.en: CBD COP16 operationalized the DSI multilateral mechanism in Cali in 2024. The Cali Fund was launched in Rome on 25 February 2025 to receive contributions from private-sector entities making commercial use of DSI. Fifty per cent of the Fund's resources are to be allocated to the self-identified needs of Indigenous peoples and local communities, including women and youth. These dates and financial arrangements are current-affairs facts and should be checked against the latest CBD decision before an examination.
paragraphs.te: CBD COP16, 2024లో Caliలో DSI multilateral mechanismను operationalize చేసింది. DSIను commercially use చేసే private-sector entities నుంచి contributions receive చేయడానికి Cali Fundను 25 February 2025న Romeలో launch చేశారు. Fund resourcesలో 50%ను Indigenous peoples మరియు local communities తమకు తాము identify చేసుకున్న needsకు allocate చేయాలి; ఇందులో women, youth కూడా ఉంటారు. ఇవి current-affairs facts కాబట్టి examకు ముందు latest CBD decisionతో re-check చేయాలి.

title.en: CITES, CMS and Ramsar: Species, Trade and Wetlands
title.te: CITES, CMS, Ramsar: Species, Trade మరియు Wetlands

paragraphs.en: International conservation conventions divide work by subject. CITES regulates international wildlife trade, CMS coordinates the conservation of migratory species across their range, and Ramsar provides the international framework for wetland conservation and wise use. For each convention, an exam answer should identify what it protects, how its listing system works, and which authorities or institutions implement it.
paragraphs.te: International conservation Conventions అన్నీ ఒకే పని చేయవు. CITES international wildlife tradeను regulate చేస్తుంది. CMS, migratory species ప్రయాణించే rangeలో countries మధ్య conservationను coordinate చేస్తుంది. Ramsar, wetlands conservation మరియు wise useకు international framework ఇస్తుంది. ప్రతి Conventionను చదివేటప్పుడు మూడు questions అడగాలి: అది దేనిని protect చేస్తుంది? దాని listing system ఎలా పనిచేస్తుంది? దాన్ని ఏ authorities లేదా institutions implement చేస్తాయి?

paragraphs.en: CITES entered into force on 1 July 1975. It is an independent convention, not a protocol under the CBD. Its purpose is to ensure that international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten their survival. A specimen may be a live or dead animal or plant, or a recognizable part or derivative covered by the Convention.
paragraphs.te: CITES 1 July 1975న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. ఇది CBD కింద Protocol కాదు; independent Convention. Wild animals, plants specimensలో జరిగే international trade, వాటి survivalకు threat కాకుండా చూడటం దీని purpose. Specimen అంటే live లేదా dead animal/plant మాత్రమే కాదు; Convention cover చేసే recognizable part లేదా derivative కూడా కావచ్చు.

paragraphs.en: CITES Appendix I contains species threatened with extinction that are or may be affected by trade. International trade in wild-sourced specimens for primarily commercial purposes is generally prohibited; other trade is allowed only in exceptional cases under both import and export controls. Certain specimens bred in captivity or artificially propagated for commercial purposes may be treated under Appendix-II rules. Thus, Appendix I does not mean that every movement of every specimen is absolutely prohibited.
paragraphs.te: CITES Appendix Iలో extinction threat ఎదుర్కొంటున్న, trade వల్ల ప్రభావితం అయ్యే లేదా అయ్యే అవకాశం ఉన్న species ఉంటాయి. Wild-sourced specimensను primarily commercial purpose కోసం international trade చేయడం సాధారణంగా prohibited. ఇతర trade exceptional casesలో import, export controlsతో మాత్రమే జరుగుతుంది. Commercial purpose కోసం captive breeding చేసిన animals లేదా artificially propagated plantsకు చెందిన కొన్ని specimensను Appendix-II rules ప్రకారం treat చేయవచ్చు. కాబట్టి Appendix I అంటే ప్రతి specimen movement పూర్తిగా prohibited అని కాదు.

paragraphs.en: Appendix II includes species that are not necessarily threatened with extinction now but may become so unless trade is strictly regulated; it also includes certain look-alike species needed for effective control. An export permit requires the exporting State's Scientific Authority to make a non-detriment finding (NDF), meaning the export will not be detrimental to the survival of the species, and its Management Authority must be satisfied that the specimen was legally acquired. CITES itself normally does not require an import permit for Appendix-II specimens, though a country may impose stricter domestic rules.
paragraphs.te: Appendix IIలో ప్రస్తుతం extinction threat తప్పనిసరిగా లేకపోయినా, trade strictగా regulate చేయకపోతే threatలోకి వెళ్లే species ఉంటాయి. Effective control కోసం కొన్ని look-alike species కూడా ఇందులో ఉంటాయి. Export permit ఇవ్వడానికి, export వల్ల species survivalకు harm ఉండదని exporting State Scientific Authority ఒక Non-Detriment Finding (NDF) ఇవ్వాలి. Specimen legally acquire అయిందని Management Authority satisfy కావాలి. Appendix-II importకు CITES సాధారణంగా import permit కోరదు; కానీ ఒక country తన domestic lawలో stricter rules పెట్టవచ్చు.

paragraphs.en: Appendix III contains a species that one Party already regulates within its jurisdiction and for which it seeks cooperation from other Parties to control international trade. Export from the listing State requires an export permit. Export from another range State requires a certificate of origin, while re-export requires a re-export certificate. Appendix III is therefore a cooperation mechanism initiated by an individual Party, unlike Appendices I and II, whose amendments are decided collectively by the Conference of the Parties.
paragraphs.te: Appendix IIIలో, ఒక Party తన jurisdictionలో ఇప్పటికే regulate చేస్తున్న speciesను list చేసి, international trade control కోసం ఇతర Parties cooperation కోరుతుంది. Listing State నుంచి exportకు export permit అవసరం. మరో range State నుంచి exportకు certificate of origin అవసరం; re-exportకు re-export certificate అవసరం. అందువల్ల Appendix III ఒక individual Party initiate చేసే cooperation mechanism. Appendices I, II amendmentsను మాత్రం Conference of the Parties collectively decide చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: Each CITES Party designates at least one Management Authority and at least one Scientific Authority. The Management Authority administers the permit and certificate system. The Scientific Authority advises whether trade would harm the species and makes the NDF where required. For an Appendix-I import permit, the importing Scientific Authority must advise that the import will not be detrimental; for a living specimen it must also be satisfied that the proposed recipient is suitably equipped to house and care for it. The importing Management Authority must be satisfied that the specimen will not be used for primarily commercial purposes.
paragraphs.te: ప్రతి CITES Party కనీసం ఒక Management Authority, ఒక Scientific Authorityను designate చేస్తుంది. Management Authority permits, certificates systemను administer చేస్తుంది. Trade వల్ల speciesకు harm జరుగుతుందా అని Scientific Authority advice ఇస్తుంది; అవసరమైనప్పుడు NDF తయారు చేస్తుంది. Appendix-I import permit కోసం, import speciesకు detrimental కాదని importing Scientific Authority advise చేయాలి. Living specimen అయితే recipient దాన్ని properly house చేసి care చేయగలడని కూడా satisfy కావాలి. Specimen primarily commercial purposeకు use కాదని importing Management Authority satisfy కావాలి.

paragraphs.en: Introduction from the sea means transporting into a State a specimen taken in a marine area beyond the jurisdiction of any State. For specimens of Appendix-I and Appendix-II species, the Scientific Authority of the State of introduction must make an NDF before the required certificate is issued. Appendix-I specimens also face the additional non-commercial-purpose condition. Introduction-from-the-sea rules do not apply to Appendix III.
paragraphs.te: ఏ country jurisdictionకూ చెందని marine area నుంచి specimenను తీసుకుని ఒక Stateలోకి transport చేయడాన్ని Introduction from the Sea అంటారు. Appendix-I, Appendix-II species specimensకు required certificate issue చేసే ముందు State of introduction Scientific Authority NDF ఇవ్వాలి. Appendix-I specimenకు additionalగా non-commercial-purpose condition కూడా ఉంటుంది. Introduction-from-the-Sea rules Appendix IIIకు వర్తించవు.

paragraphs.en: For Appendix-II species subject to trade levels that may be unsustainable, the CITES Animals Committee and Plants Committee conduct the Review of Significant Trade. They study biological and trade information and recommend corrective measures. If the Party concerned does not implement adequate measures, the matter may reach the Standing Committee, which can recommend suspension of trade in specimens of the species concerned. The scientific committees examine sustainability; the Standing Committee handles the compliance response.
paragraphs.te: Appendix-II speciesలో trade level unsustainableగా ఉండవచ్చని concern వచ్చినప్పుడు, CITES Animals Committee మరియు Plants Committee Review of Significant Trade నిర్వహిస్తాయి. Biological, trade informationను examine చేసి corrective measures recommend చేస్తాయి. Concerned Party adequate measures తీసుకోకపోతే issue Standing Committeeకు వెళ్లవచ్చు. అది concerned species specimens tradeను suspend చేయాలని recommend చేయగలదు. అంటే scientific committees sustainabilityను examine చేస్తాయి; Standing Committee compliance responseను handle చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: The IUCN Red List, CITES Appendices and the Schedules under India's Wild Life (Protection) Act answer different questions. The Red List assesses extinction risk scientifically. CITES Appendices determine international-trade controls. The Indian Act's Schedules determine domestic legal protection. A species moving to a different Red List category does not automatically move between CITES Appendices or Indian legal Schedules.
paragraphs.te: IUCN Red List, CITES Appendices, India's Wild Life (Protection) Act Schedules వేర్వేరు questionsకు answers ఇస్తాయి. Red List extinction riskను scientifically assess చేస్తుంది. CITES Appendices international-trade controlsను నిర్ణయిస్తాయి. Indian Act Schedules domestic legal protectionను నిర్ణయిస్తాయి. Red Listలో category మారినంత మాత్రాన CITES Appendix లేదా Indian legal Schedule automaticగా మారదు.

paragraphs.en: The Convention on Migratory Species (CMS), also called the Bonn Convention, was concluded in 1979 and entered into force on 1 November 1983. Migratory animals cross national boundaries or move through areas under different jurisdictions, so one country acting alone may not protect them throughout their life cycle. CMS therefore coordinates conservation among Range States.
paragraphs.te: Convention on Migratory Species (CMS)ను Bonn Convention అని కూడా అంటారు. ఇది 1979లో conclude అయింది; 1 November 1983న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. Migratory animals national boundaries దాటుతాయి లేదా different jurisdictionsలో travel చేస్తాయి. కాబట్టి ఒక country action alone వాటి entire life cycleను protect చేయలేకపోవచ్చు. అందుకే CMS, Range States మధ్య conservationను coordinate చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: CMS Appendix I lists migratory species that are endangered and calls for strict protection, conservation or restoration of important habitats, removal of migration obstacles where appropriate, and control of other endangering factors. Appendix II lists migratory species that have an unfavourable conservation status and need international agreements, or whose conservation would significantly benefit from international cooperation. Cooperation may take the form of legally binding Agreements or non-binding Memoranda of Understanding. CMS Appendix I must not be confused with CITES Appendix I: one concerns migratory-species conservation, the other international-trade control.
paragraphs.te: CMS Appendix Iలో endangered migratory species ఉంటాయి. వాటికి strict protection ఇవ్వడం, important habitatsను conserve లేదా restore చేయడం, అవసరమైనప్పుడు migration obstacles తొలగించడం, ఇతర threatsను control చేయడం దీని focus. Appendix IIలో unfavourable conservation status ఉన్న, international agreement అవసరమైన species లేదా cooperation వల్ల significantly benefit అయ్యే species ఉంటాయి. Cooperation legally binding Agreements ద్వారా లేదా non-binding Memoranda of Understanding ద్వారా జరగవచ్చు. CMS Appendix Iను CITES Appendix Iతో confuse చేయకూడదు: మొదటిది migratory-species conservation; రెండవది international-trade control.

paragraphs.en: Current-affairs note: CMS COP15 was held from 23 to 29 March 2026 in Campo Grande, Brazil. It decided to add 40 taxa to the CMS Appendices. Under Article XI(5), the amendments entered into force on 27 June 2026, except for a Party entering a reservation in accordance with the Convention. In an exam, write 40 taxa—not automatically 40 species—and attach the date to COP15.
paragraphs.te: Current-affairs note: CMS COP15, 23–29 March 2026లో Brazilలోని Campo Grandeలో జరిగింది. CMS Appendicesకు 40 taxaను add చేయాలని నిర్ణయించింది. Article XI(5) ప్రకారం, Convention rulesకు అనుగుణంగా reservation పెట్టిన Party తప్ప, amendments 27 June 2026న అమల్లోకి వచ్చాయి. Examలో 40 taxa అని రాయాలి; automaticగా 40 speciesగా మార్చకూడదు. ఈ figureను CMS COP15 dateతో కలిపి గుర్తుంచుకోవాలి.

paragraphs.en: The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was adopted at Ramsar, Iran, on 2 February 1971 and entered into force on 21 December 1975. For this reason, 2 February is observed as World Wetlands Day. The Convention promotes the conservation and wise use of wetlands through national action and international cooperation.
paragraphs.te: Ramsar Convention on Wetlandsను Iranలోని Ramsarలో 2 February 1971న adopt చేశారు; ఇది 21 December 1975న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. అందుకే 2 Februaryను World Wetlands Dayగా observe చేస్తారు. National action మరియు international cooperation ద్వారా wetlands conservation, wise useను promote చేయడం ఈ Convention purpose.

paragraphs.en: A wetland qualifies for designation as a Ramsar Site when it meets at least one of the Convention's nine criteria and the Party designates it for the List of Wetlands of International Importance. Ramsar's wise-use principle applies to all wetlands within a Party's territory, not only listed sites. Wise use means maintaining ecological character through ecosystem approaches within the context of sustainable development. Ramsar listing does not prohibit every form of human use, and it does not automatically create a domestic protected-area category.
paragraphs.te: ఒక wetland, Conventionలోని nine criteriaలో కనీసం one criterion meet చేసి, concerned Party దాన్ని List of Wetlands of International Importanceకు designate చేసినప్పుడు Ramsar Site అవుతుంది. Ramsar wise-use principle listed sitesకే కాదు; Party territoryలోని all wetlandsకు వర్తిస్తుంది. Wise use అంటే sustainable development contextలో ecosystem approaches ఉపయోగించి wetland ecological characterను maintain చేయడం. Ecological character అంటే wetlandకు ప్రత్యేకత ఇచ్చే natural components, processes, functions కొనసాగుతున్న స్థితి. Ramsar listing వల్ల every human use prohibit కాదు; domestic law కింద protected-area category automaticగా ఏర్పడదు.

paragraphs.en: India's first Ramsar Sites were Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park, both designated on 1 October 1981. The number and total area of India's Ramsar Sites change when new sites are added or boundaries are revised, so such figures must always carry a reference date. Rankings based on site number or area should also be treated as current-affairs data, not timeless facts.
paragraphs.te: Indiaలో first Ramsar Sites, Chilika Lake మరియు Keoladeo National Park. రెండింటినీ 1 October 1981న designate చేశారు. New sites add అయినప్పుడు లేదా boundaries revise అయినప్పుడు India Ramsar Sites number, total area మారతాయి. కాబట్టి ఈ figuresకు reference date తప్పనిసరిగా ఇవ్వాలి. Site number లేదా area ఆధారంగా చెప్పే rankings కూడా current-affairs data; timeless facts కావు.

paragraphs.en: The Montreux Record is a register of Ramsar Sites where human interference has caused, is causing or is likely to cause a change in ecological character. Inclusion is a warning that priority conservation attention is needed, not an additional honour. Removal from the Record does not cancel Ramsar designation. Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake remain on the Record, while Chilika Lake was removed in 2002 after restoration improved its hydrology and ecological character.
paragraphs.te: Montreux Record అనేది Ramsar Sitesలోని ఒక special register. Human interference వల్ల ecological character మారిన, మారుతున్న లేదా మారే అవకాశం ఉన్న sitesను ఇందులో include చేస్తారు. ఇందులో inclusion additional honour కాదు; siteకు priority conservation attention అవసరమని warning. Record నుంచి remove చేసినా Ramsar designation cancel కాదు. Keoladeo National Park, Loktak Lake ఇంకా Recordలో ఉన్నాయి. Restoration వల్ల hydrology, ecological character improve అయిన తర్వాత Chilika Lakeను 2002లో Record నుంచి remove చేశారు.
